excerpt: The Lorapok-Inventory-System README describes a multi-tenant point of sale where each shop has its own subdomain, branding, and database.
content:
# Lorapok Inventory System

The public repository [Maijied/Lorapok-Inventory-System](https://github.com/Maijied/Lorapok-Inventory-System) is a PHP application. GitHub reports the language as PHP, and the repository homepage is [maijied.github.io/Lorapok-Inventory-System](https://maijied.github.io/Lorapok-Inventory-System/).

## What the README says

The README titles the project Lorapok Retail and describes it as multi-tenant inventory and point-of-sale software for shops that sell serialised goods. One super admin provisions shops. Each shop gets its own subdomain, its own branding, and its own database.

## What this note does not claim

This note does not report install counts, revenue, or uptime. Those figures are not in the public repository description. The useful fact is the tenancy model: shop data is separated by database, not only by a tenant column.

## Where to look

- Source: https://github.com/Maijied/Lorapok-Inventory-System
- Site linked from the repository: https://maijied.github.io/Lorapok-Inventory-System/

title: MindNode encrypts notes in the browser before they are stored
excerpt: The MindNode README describes a key-based notepad that encrypts notes with the Web Crypto API and does not keep server-side keys.
content:
# Lorapok MindNode

[Maijied/Lorapok-MindNode](https://github.com/Maijied/Lorapok-MindNode) is a JavaScript project. Its homepage is [maijied.github.io/Lorapok-MindNode](https://maijied.github.io/Lorapok-MindNode/).

## What the README says

The README calls MindNode a high-security, key-based digital notepad with end-to-end encryption. It states that there are no accounts and no server-side keys, and that notes are encrypted in the browser before they leave the device. The listed mechanism is the Web Crypto API, using PBKDF2 and AES-GCM.

## Why that distinction matters

A notepad that encrypts after upload is a different product from one that encrypts before upload. The README places the encryption step in the browser and says the server does not hold the keys. Anyone evaluating the project should read that section in the repository rather than treat this note as a security audit.

## Where to look

- Source: https://github.com/Maijied/Lorapok-MindNode
- Site: https://maijied.github.io/Lorapok-MindNode/

The organization repository homepage points at [maijied.github.io/Lorapok-API_Atlas](https://maijied.github.io/Lorapok-API_Atlas/). The repository description says the directory lists 2100+ public APIs. That number is the project's own catalog claim. It is not a count of Lorapok-owned APIs, and this site no longer shows it as a lab-wide statistic.

# Loragent

[Maijied/Loragent](https://github.com/Maijied/Loragent) is a JavaScript repository. Its homepage is [loragent.lorapok.tech](https://loragent.lorapok.tech/).

## What the README says

The README presents Loragent as a multi-agent orchestration framework for IDE agents, naming Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Antigravity, Roo Code, Cline, Zed, and Codex. It describes turning a single-agent IDE into a specialist software firm.

## The count on this website

`src/data/agents-index.json` in the Lorapok website repository declares `"total": 224`, and the formations in that file add up to 224 skill definitions (210 auto, 2 orchestrator, 9 freelance, 3 observer). That is a count of catalog entries in this repo. It is not a count of people using the software.

The README also uses the phrase "250-resource AI marketplace." This site uses the counted index total, 224, wherever it states a number.

## Where to look

content:
# FreqGhost

[Maijied/FreqGhost](https://github.com/Maijied/FreqGhost) is a Python repository. The README title is "FreqGhost: WiFi DensePose Sensing Observatory."

## What the README says

FreqGhost is described as a WiFi sensing and live 3D visualization platform inspired by WiFi DensePose. The README says it detects human presence, maps physical motion, and extracts respiration and heart rate from distortion of WiFi radio frequencies, specifically channel state information, including through walls.

That is the project's stated design. This note does not add accuracy percentages or clinical claims. If you need the sensing method, read the repository.

## Where to look
